# Switchyard — forward manifest for Claude Design

**Status:** open asks, written 2026-09-09 against `main` at the Switchyard
layout pass.
**Audience:** Claude Design. This is a request list, not a change log — nothing
here has been altered in the delivered art.
**Companion files:** `docs/forward-manifest.json` (design's own, generated by
the export — these asks want to appear there next drop), `docs/DESIGN-BRIEF.md`
§3.6, `docs/design-system/README.md` (running list of code-vs-design gaps).

---

## Why this document exists

Switchyard has been rebuilt three times. Each pass fixed a real problem and
each one uncovered a deeper one, and every time the deeper problem turned out
to be the same shape: **a module that tiles was carrying detail that should
punctuate.**

The kit itself is good. The ballast reads as ballast, the wagons read as
wagons, the retaining wall is exactly what a yard boundary looks like. What
went wrong was never the drawing — it was that pieces meant to repeat every
four metres contain features that a real railway puts down every forty, and
that a piece of scenery drawn *into the ground plane* becomes the dominant
feature of the map once the ground is tiled twenty-four times.

So the largest ask here is not new art. It is **separating what repeats from
what punctuates**, and one export bug.

---

## The rule underneath almost all of it

> A tiling module may only contain features that are true at its own repeat
> distance.

Three delivered pieces break it, and between them they account for most of why
this map has been unreadable:

| Module | Repeat | Feature baked in | What the player saw |
|---|---|---|---|
| `switchyard_terrain` | 20 m, 6×4 grid | two "disused sidings" at local z ±6 | **eight full-width tracks across the whole map** on a grid — through the lanes, the tower pads and the spawn, with no throat, no turnout and no buffer at either end |
| `switchyard_path_ground` | 4 m, along every road and lane | `lane_marker` + `lane_marker_cap` (a mile-marker post) | a marker post **every four metres**, hundreds of them, along every track and every haul road |
| `switchyard_cut_channel` | 4 m, along the cutting | `cut_lamp_post` + `cut_lamp` | a lamp **every four metres** down a twelve-metre cutting |

The sidings were the worst of the three because there were more of them than
there was real track, so the deliberately-laid yard — one lead, three roads,
turnouts in order, buffer stops — was invisible inside the hash. That is the
literal answer to "the railways and switches don't make a lot of sense": the
switches were there, and eight tracks that had none were drawn on top of them.

**All three are currently worked around in code by hiding nodes** — which is a
patch, not a fix, and it silently loses detail that should be on the map
somewhere:

- `GameRoot.cs` hides `terrain_siding-6` / `terrain_siding6` on every tile
- `GameRoot.cs` hides `lane_track` on the haul road (see ask **D**)
- `MapKit.ThinOut` keeps `lane_marker` and `cut_lamp_post` on one module in five

---

## P0 — the export bug

### A. Ship all four terrain variants

`switchyard_terrain.buildVariant(K, v)` draws four variants and the note
describes all four:

| v | detail |
|---|---|
| 0 | standing water + weed tufts |
| 1 | **switch stand** + tufts + puddle |
| 2 | cable trough + tufts |
| 3 | puddle + dropped sleepers + tufts |

The exporter calls `build()`, which is `buildVariant(K, 0)`. **Only v0 has ever
existed as a GLB.** Confirmed by reading the node table of the shipped file:
it contains `terrain_puddle` and `terrain_tufts_*` and nothing else from that
list.

Two consequences, both of which we have been fighting:

1. **The ground repeats.** One tile laid twenty-four times puts the same puddle
   in the same place on a perfect lattice. We currently mitigate by turning
   alternate tiles a half-turn, which helps and is not a fix.
2. **The switch stand has never been delivered.** The lever and target that
   work a turnout exist only inside v1. Code that hid stray stands from the
   tiles was hiding a node that is not in the file — it had been a no-op since
   it was written.

**Ask:** export `switchyard_terrain_v1`, `_v2`, `_v3` as their own files
alongside `switchyard_terrain`. We will cycle them across the tile grid, which
fixes the repetition properly.

This is the single highest-value item in this document. It is not a redraw —
the art is already written.

---

## P1 — split what tiles from what punctuates

### B. Sidings out of the terrain tile

**Ask:** `switchyard_siding.glb` — one 20 m length of disused track (rusted
rail, weathered sleepers, ballast staining), as its own piece. Remove
`terrain_siding-6` / `terrain_siding6` from the terrain tile.

We will place sidings where a siding belongs, in ones and twos. Ground is
ground; track is track. Nothing that is laid on the ground should be part of
the ground.

### C. Occasional details out of the linear modules

**Ask:** pull these out into their own props and remove them from the modules
that tile:

| New file | Taken from | Real-world spacing |
|---|---|---|
| `switchyard_dress_lamp.glb` | `cut_lamp_post` + `cut_lamp` in `switchyard_cut_channel` | 25–50 m |
| `switchyard_dress_milepost.glb` | `lane_marker` + `lane_marker_cap` in `switchyard_path_ground` | a mile, or a yard-road identity plate at the road head |

Both are nice pieces of detail. They just cannot live in something that repeats
every four metres.

### D. Split the lane module in two

`switchyard_path_ground` is described as the yard's haul road and carries
`lane_track` — a rail — down its centre. Switchyard needs both things and they
are not the same thing:

- **the haul road**: where players and enemies walk. Ballast, kerbs, no rail.
- **the running line**: where trains go. Sleepers and rail.

We currently instantiate the one module twice and hide `lane_track` for the
road version. That works, but it means the road and the track are drawn to the
same 3.4 m width, and a haul road and a single-track formation are not the same
width in life.

**Ask:** `switchyard_path_ground.glb` keeps the road (no rail, 3.4 m), and
`switchyard_track.glb` is a 4 m length of plain track (sleepers, rail,
ballast shoulder, ~2.6 m over the shoulders). Both run **along +X**, both
repeat at 4 m.

---

## P2 — pieces the map currently grayboxes

Each of these is built in code out of coloured boxes plus a borrowed module.
They function; they do not look like design drew them.

### E. Turnout / points — `switchyard_turnout.glb`

The one piece a yard cannot read without. We lay a lead and lay roads off it,
and where they meet there is nothing but two beds of track overlapping.

- **Ratio 1:6.** This matters and it is measured: the ladder is a straight
  lead, and a ladder's angle *is* its turnout angle. Ours was 1:4.9, sharper
  than any turnout ever laid, and it is now stretched to exactly **1:6.0** —
  which is a short-radius yard turnout, prototypical for somewhere nothing
  moves fast. The railway probe fails the build if it ever drifts below 1:6.
- Straight route along +X, diverging route leaving to +Z at 1:6.
- Length ~12 m so it spans the divergence; origin at the toe of the points.
- Switch stand on the +X side (or ship it separately per **A**).

### F. Cutting ends — `switchyard_cut_headwall.glb`

`switchyard_cut_channel` tiles beautifully now that it is laid along its own
axis, but a cutting that simply stops is a wall someone dropped. It wants an
end: a headwall / wing walls where the kerb walls meet grade.

- Same 6 m lane width and 1.2 m wall height as the channel, so it butts.
- One file, mirrored by yaw for the far end.

The cutting is 12 m long on the current map — the longest stretch of the
shortcut that is genuinely clear of every socket and of the other ground route.
That window is x −18…−10, which is **exactly the placement your own note on
`switchyard_cut_channel` specifies**. Two independent derivations agreeing is a
good sign; please keep the note, it is doing real work.

### G. Overbridge — `switchyard_overbridge.glb`

Currently: `switchyard_middeck` laid across two graybox piers.

- Deck 5 m wide, spanning ~17 m, soffit at **7 m** above rail (a real structure
  over a railway is held to about 22 ft).
- Plate girders or a lattice truss, parapets, and piers outside the outermost
  track.
- Note: `switchyard_bridge_intact` / `switchyard_bridge_collapsed` are already
  M4 entries in `forward-manifest.json` for the map morph. **If those are the
  same bridge, say so and we will build the overbridge from them now** rather
  than commissioning a second one.

### H. Tunnel portal — `switchyard_portal.glb`

Currently: two `switchyard_retainingwall` abutments and a graybox header.

- A portal the running line disappears into where it leaves the map: arch or
  square-headed, wing walls, a date stone or a line plate.
- Clear opening about 5 m wide × 5.5 m high — the graybox we run today is
  4 × 5.6, and 4 m is visibly tight for a double-track-looking formation.
  Overall ~12 m across.
- Three needed on the current map: the running line east and west, and the
  depot road west.

## Conventions we need stated on delivery

One of the three passes was spent on a bug that a single field in the manifest
would have prevented. `switchyard_cut_channel` runs **4 m along its local +X**
with the lane across **Z**; it was placed with a helper that aligns **+Z**, so
every module sat a quarter-turn wrong — its track running across the lane, its
kerb walls straddling it — and was stepped by the module's 9.6 m width instead
of its 4 m length. Nine of those end to end is not a cutting; it is a row of
concrete gates over the shortcut, and it survived a review because it is
perfectly plausible art placed perfectly wrongly.

**Ask: every linear module carries its run axis and repeat length**, e.g.

```json
{
  "id": "switchyard_cut_channel",
  "run": "+X",
  "repeat": 4.0,
  "width": 9.6,
  "note": "…"
}
```

`run` and `repeat` are the two facts a placement needs and neither is
recoverable from the file. `width` lets us check clearances without opening the
mesh.

The existing conventions block (metres, +Y up, −Z forward, origin at feet /
grip / footprint centre) is right and unambiguous for standalone props. It is
linear modules it does not cover.

---

## The map, so pieces are drawn to fit

Current geometry, from `GameRoot.cs`. Everything below is in metres, +X east,
+Z north, y 0 at yard grade.

| | |
|---|---|
| Ground slab | 110 × 80, so x ±55 and z ±40 |
| **Playfield** (every ground socket, both ground routes, the spawn) | **z −18 … +16** |
| Running line | z 20.5, x −46 → 44, portals at x −45 and 43 |
| Classification roads A / B / C | z 24.5 / 28 / 31.5, buffer stops at x 37 |
| Lead | (−42, 20.5) → (24, 31.5) — **1:6.0** |
| Turnouts | road A at x −18, road B at x 3, road C at x 24 |
| Depot road (serves the spawn dock) | z −32, x −44 → 24, portal at x −45 |
| Perimeter retaining wall | z +35 and z −37 |
| Overbridges | x −30 and x 30, spanning z 18.5 → 35, deck at y 7 |
| Freight cut | x −18 → −10, along the shortcut route, b1 at (−8, −1) |
| Mid deck / upper catwalk | y 5 and y 10 |

The hard constraint is that **no track may pass within 3 m of a tower socket, a
walked route, the spawn, the armory or a hero station**. That is not a style
preference — a running line through four tower pads and a depot road four
metres from the spawn were both shipped, because both photograph perfectly well
as a railway. `--shot switchyard <txt> railway` measures it now and fails the
build, and it runs in CI.

---

## Already right — please do not change

- `switchyard_retainingwall` — exactly what a yard boundary looks like, and it
  doubles as the map perimeter as the note says.
- `switchyard_dress_railcar`, `_container`, `_buffer` — all three sit correctly,
  read at distance, and tile in rakes without interpenetrating at 12.6 m.
- `switchyard_dress_signaltower` — good, and the 8 m mast is the right call. It
  is why we place only four: at the throat, at one turnout, at the yard's east
  exit, and one on the depot road. One per turnout would be a forest in a 15 m
  band.
- `switchyard_cut_channel` itself — the geometry is right, the note is right,
  and it was the placement that was wrong. It only wants its lamp taken out
  (**C**) and an end piece (**F**).
- The ballast bed and its texture set. Once the sidings come out of it, it is
  doing exactly the job it should.

`icon_path_field` · `icon_path_analysis` · `icon_path_ramp` · `icon_path_peak` ·

## How we will know it landed

| Check | Command |
|---|---|
| Names match the brief | `make assets` |
| Nothing delivered goes unused | `make usage` |
| Nothing requested is missing | `--asset-audit` |
| No track through anything a player stands on, ladder still 1:6 | `--shot switchyard <txt> railway` |
| Every climb lands on something | `--shot switchyard <txt> traversal` |
| Eye-level read of the two railway features | `--shot switchyard <png> cut` and `… yardline` |

The last one is the one that matters for this document. The others can all pass
on a map that makes no sense.
